index.follow-the-conversation-at-2: Follow the conversation at the table.
index.seal-speak-shows-what-2: Seal Speak shows what the people around you are saying, as they say it, in large clear text. It all happens on your iPhone, so it works with no internet.

index.a-working-demo-of: A working demo of Seal Speak
index.this-demo-plays-a: This demo plays a made-up conversation. Tap Start captions, then ✕ to pause. Try [ Save ], tap the dim to read, open the list icon for saved conversations, and the gear for Settings.
index.everyone-deserves-to-be: Everyone deserves to be part of the conversation.
index.i-built-seal-speak: I built Seal Speak as a birthday gift for my mom, who is hard of hearing. Now it's here for you too.
index.if-it-helps-you: If it helps you stay close to the people you love, it's for you.

index.put-your-phone-on: Put your phone on the table
index.open-seal-speak-and: Open Seal Speak and tap Start captions. Words show up as people talk.
index.when-the-voice-changes: When the voice changes, Seal starts a new line and labels it Speaker 1 or Speaker 2. Sounds like laughter or a doorbell show up as short labels.

index.never-recorded-the-sound: Never recordedThe sound is turned into words, then gone.
index.no-internet-works-in: No internetWorks in airplane mode after a one-time setup.
index.no-account-no-ads: No accountNo ads, no tracking. Privacy policy
index.made-to-be-easy: Made to be easy to read
index.everything-on-screen-fades: Everything on screen fades in and out. Nothing slides around while you read.
index.a-caption-shown-in: A caption shown in each of Seal's color themes and letterings
index.follows-your-phone-s: Follows your phone's text size, with A− and A+ to go bigger or smaller.
index.three-light-and-three: Three light and three dark. Every one keeps strong contrast between the words and the background.
index.opendyslexic-atkinson-hyperlegible: OpenDyslexic, Atkinson Hyperlegible, Standard, Rounded, Serif and Typewriter. Pick whichever is most comfortable.
index.why-seal-looks-and: Why Seal looks and works this way
index.the-choices-behind-the: The choices behind the design, and where they come from.
index.contrast-between-light-and: Contrast between light and dark matters most
index.readers-with-low-vision: Readers with low vision read better with strong brightness contrast than with color contrast alone. So every theme is built for brightness contrast, and a test makes sure each one reaches at least 7:1.
index.you-choose-the-size: You choose the size, lettering and colors
index.caption-size-lettering-spacing: Caption size, lettering, spacing and the contrast between caption and background all affect how easy captions are to read. Seal lets you change the size, the lettering and the colors.
index.source-a-caption-readability: Source: a caption readability study with older TV viewers, Sun Repository.
index.research-found-dark-text: Research found dark text on a light background read a little better, with a smaller difference for older adults, and dark mode caused no extra eye strain. Both work, so Seal offers three of each instead of choosing for you.
index.source-piepenbrock-et-al: Source: Piepenbrock et al. (2013), summarised by the Nielsen Norman Group. The study was with people with healthy eyes.
index.seal-s-default-lettering: Seal's default lettering is OpenDyslexic. Studies haven't shown it makes reading faster or more accurate, so it's offered because some people find it comfortable, alongside Atkinson Hyperlegible (designed by the Braille Institute for low vision) and four others.
index.speech-to-text-uses: Speech-to-text uses Apple's on-device speech recognition. Telling voices apart uses the open-source FluidAudio library and NVIDIA's Sortformer model, bundled in the app so nothing goes over the network.
index.we-don-t-guess: We don't guess which parts work best. We try each option on the same real recordings and count the mistakes.
index.hours-of-real-conversations: hours of real conversations, from 122 people with accents from all over the world
index.fewer-mistakes-in-english: fewer mistakes in English with the caption engine coming in 1.1
index.for-a-word-to: for a word to show, against 0.67 s today (median, on a Mac)

index.mistakes-in-every-100: Mistakes in every 100 words, English conversations
index.lower-is-better-17: Lower is better. 17,528 clips of people talking, the same clips for both.
index.captions-are-english-only: Captions are English only today. Before offering more languages, we measured them. In Spanish, French and German, Parakeet made 30 to 40% fewer mistakes than Apple.
index.mistakes-in-every-100-3: Mistakes in every 100 words, by language
index.these-are-people-reading: These are people reading sentences aloud in a quiet room, so every engine does better here than in a real conversation.
index.for-the-curious-how: For the curious: how we tested

index.timing-526-clips-45: Timing: 526 clips (45 minutes) fed in as if live. "Correct word" is when a word first shows correctly, measured from when it was said.
index.word-error-rate-and: Word error rate and timing by engine
index.fleurs-test-sets-cc: FLEURS test sets (CC BY 4.0): read speech, 908 Spanish, 676 French and German clips. Accent marks count: esta for está is a mistake.
index.spanish-4-0-3: Spanish 4.0% (3.4 to 4.5) against 2.8% (2.4 to 3.3); French 7.5% (6.7 to 8.3) against 4.5% (3.9 to 5.1); German 7.2% (6.5 to 7.9) against 4.4% (3.8 to 5.0). The ranges don't overlap.

privacy.seal-shows-live-captions: Seal shows live captions on your device. It collects nothing and sends nothing anywhere.
privacy.in-short-seal-runs: In short: Seal runs entirely on your device. It does not collect, store on any server, share, or sell any information about you or the people around you. There is no account, no advertising, no analytics and no tracking.
privacy.what-seal-does-with: What Seal does with the microphone
privacy.seal-listens-through-your:
Seal listens through your device's microphone only while you are captioning. The sound is turned
  into text on your device, as it happens, and is then discarded. Seal never records or keeps the audio,
  and never sends it anywhere.
privacy.speech-is-turned-into:
Speech is turned into text by Apple's speech recognition, running on your device. Telling voices
  apart ("Speaker 1", "Speaker 2") is also done on your device, by a model built into the app.
privacy.saved-conversations-when-you: Saved conversations. When you tap [ Save ], the text of that conversation is kept on your device so you can read it again. Each one is deleted automatically after 30 days, and you can delete any or all of them sooner. They are left out of iCloud and device backups and are never synced.
privacy.your-settings-such-as: Your settings, such as text size and colours, stay on your device.
privacy.deleting-the-app-deletes: Deleting the app deletes all of this.
privacy.nothing-unless-you-choose:
Nothing, unless you choose to send it. If you tap Copy or Share, the conversation text goes only
  where you send it (for example a message or a note), and from then on that app's privacy terms apply.
privacy.the-first-time-you: The first time you use Seal, your device may download Apple's speech-recognition language files. Apple provides that download, not Seal, and it is covered by Apple's privacy policy. After that, captioning works with no internet connection at all.
privacy.no-advertising-analytics-crash: No advertising, analytics, crash reporting or tracking of any kind.
privacy.no-selling-or-sharing: No selling or sharing of data, because there is no data to sell or share.
privacy.no-contacts-location-photos: No contacts, location, photos or camera access.
privacy.seal-is-not-directed: Seal is not directed at children and collects no personal information from anyone, of any age.
privacy.if-this-policy-changes:
If this policy changes, the new version will be posted on this page with a new effective date.
  Any change that would make Seal collect or share information would be explained here before it
  happens.
support.help-and-answers-for: Help and answers for Seal, live captions for conversations, on your device.
support.live-captions-for-conversations: Live captions for conversations, on your device.
support.need-help-or-found: Need help or found a problem? Email gil.eskayo@icloud.com. Please say which device you use (for example iPhone 17) and what happened. Every message is read by a person.
support.only-once-the-first:
Only once. The first time you start, your device may download Apple's speech files. After that,
  Seal captions with no internet connection, including in airplane mode.
support.does-seal-record-or: Does Seal record or upload my conversations?
support.no-sound-is-turned: No. Sound is turned into text on your device and the audio is never kept. If you tap [ Save ], the text of that conversation stays on your device for 30 days so you can reread it, then it's deleted. See the privacy policy.
support.4-99-once-there: $4.99, once. There are no ads, no subscriptions and no in-app purchases.
support.which-devices-and-languages: Which devices and languages does it work with?
support.iphone-12-or-newer: iPhone 12 or newer with iOS 26 or later. Seal is iPhone only for now, and captions are in English.
support.seal-starts-a-new:
Seal starts a new line when the voice changes and labels it Speaker 1, Speaker 2. It goes by the
  sound of the voice, so it can mix people up, especially similar voices. It doesn't know who anyone is.
support.the-captions-got-a: The captions got a name or word wrong.
support.captions-come-from-your:
Captions come from your phone's speech recognition and can get words wrong, names most of all.
  For anything important, check with the person speaking.
support.the-screen-says-i: The screen says "I can't hear anything".
support.the-microphone-is-hearing:
The microphone is hearing almost nothing. Check that nothing is covering the bottom of the phone,
  and place the phone flat on the table between you and the people talking.
support.the-screen-will-say: The screen will say why. Tap Start again to carry on. If it keeps happening, please email us.
support.how-do-i-delete: How do I delete saved conversations?
support.tap-the-list-icon:
Tap the list icon at the top right of the captions. Open a conversation and tap [ Delete ], or tap
  [ Delete all ] at the bottom of the list. Saved conversations are also deleted automatically after 30 days,
  and when you delete the app.
support.how-do-i-send: How do I send a conversation to someone?
support.open-it-from-the:
Open it from the list icon and tap [ Share ]. Your iPhone's share sheet opens, so you can send the text
  to Notes, Messages, Mail, Files or AirDrop. To copy just a few words, hold a word, drag the handles,
  and tap [ Copy ].
versions.what-changed-in-each: What changed in each version of Seal Speak, and how we chose the caption engine, with the test results.
versions.what-changed-in-each-2: What changed in each version of Seal Speak, and the story behind the bigger choices. Each version says honestly where it stands: only what is on the App Store is live.

versions.one-big-button-to: One big button to start and stop.
versions.a-new-line-labelled: A new line, labelled Speaker 1 or Speaker 2, when the voice changes. It goes by the sound of the voice, so it can mix people up.
versions.text-size-that-follows: Text size that follows your phone, with A− and A+ to go bigger or smaller.
versions.six-colour-themes-and: Six colour themes, and six letterings including OpenDyslexic and Atkinson Hyperlegible.
versions.captions-scroll-on-their: Captions scroll on their own. Scroll back to reread, then tap to jump to the newest line.
versions.short-labels-for-sounds: Short labels for sounds like laughter, applause or a doorbell.
versions.tap-save-to-keep: Tap [ Save ] to keep a conversation on your phone for 30 days. Share it as text, or delete it sooner.
versions.private-captions-are-made: Private: captions are made on your phone, audio is never recorded or sent anywhere, no account, no ads, no tracking.
versions.works-with-no-internet: Works with no internet after a one-time setup.
versions.4-99-once-english: $4.99, once. English captions. iPhone 12 or newer with iOS 26 or later, or an iPad.
versions.captions-are-made-by: Captions are made by a computer and can contain mistakes. Seal Speak is not a medical device. The captions in 1.0.0 come from Apple's on-device speech recognition.
versions.a-full-screen-ipad: A full-screen iPad layout, with the captions using the whole screen.
versions.it-also-works-on: It also works on iPhone Duo, folded or open.
versions.not-on-the-app: Not on the App Store yet. No date.
versions.a-new-engine-makes: A new engine makes the captions: Parakeet Ultra instead of Apple's speech recognition. In our tests it makes fewer mistakes and the words show up sooner. The story is below.
versions.captions-in-more-languages: Captions in more languages. Parakeet understands 25 European languages: Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hungarian, Italian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Maltese, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swedish and Ukrainian. So far we have measured English, Spanish, French and German (below), and we test each of the others before switching it on.
versions.live-translation-of-the: Live translation of the captions into another language, right on your phone. It is an optional add-on: $1.99, once, as an in-app purchase. Captions in every language stay part of the app. It uses Apple's on-device translation, the most accurate engine we tested (below).
versions.it-still-works-with: It still works with no internet, and nothing leaves your device.
versions.the-app-gets-bigger: The app gets bigger: the new caption model is about 498 MB.
versions.planned-not-built-yet: Planned, not built yet. The new engine has run on a Mac; we still need to check it on an iPhone. No date.
versions.how-we-chose-the: How we chose the caption engine
versions.the-engine-is-the: The engine is the part that turns speech into words. Everything else in Seal Speak depends on it, so we tested the candidates instead of guessing.
versions.fewer-mistakes-than-apple: fewer mistakes than Apple's engine in English conversations: 13.8 in 100 words against 17.2
versions.median-wait-for-a: median wait for a correct word to show, against 0.67 s for Apple
versions.seal-speak-1-0: Seal Speak 1.0 uses Apple's speech recognition, because it was the one built to run fully on the phone. Before settling on it for good, we wanted to know if something better exists, especially for people who speak with an accent. A caption app that works for one kind of voice is not good enough.
versions.so-we-found-a: So we found a set of real conversations, checked by people, from speakers all over the world, and ran every engine on exactly the same recordings.
versions.how-the-caption-engines: How the caption engines were tested
versions.four-steps-from-top: Four steps from top to bottom. The EdAcc corpus, 31.4 hours of conversations in many English accents under a CC BY-SA licence, is split into 32 shards. Each engine runs on the same clips on two Macs. Each engine's word error rate is scored with a 95% confidence interval. A separate live latency sample of 526 clips, 45 minutes of audio, measures how soon words appear when audio is fed as if live.
versions.split-so-each-mac: split so each Mac works in pieces
versions.source-engine-accuracy-report: Source: engine accuracy report (header, Method, Live latency). Corpus: EdAcc, 122 speakers in this sample, licence CC BY-SA.
versions.we-count-a-mistake: We count a mistake the standard way: word error rate, the share of words that were wrong, missing or added. Lower is better. We aim for 15% or less (good) and treat 30% or less as acceptable. Each score comes with a 95% confidence interval, a range that shows how sure we are. When two ranges overlap a lot, the engines are close and we should not pretend one clearly wins.
versions.word-error-rate-by: Word error rate by caption engine, with 95% confidence intervals
versions.lower-is-better-parakeet: Lower is better. Parakeet Ultra 6-bit 13.8% (12.8 to 14.8). Parakeet v2 15.5% (14.5 to 16.6). sherpa-onnx 16.1% (14.9 to 17.2). Apple SpeechAnalyzer 17.2% (16.0 to 18.4). A dashed line marks the 15% target for good.
versions.show-the-numbers-as: Show the numbers as a table
versions.lower-is-better-whiskers: Lower is better. Whiskers are the 95% confidence interval. Source: engine accuracy report, Overall, Speed and Live latency tables. 17,528 clips, 31.4 hours, all four engines on the same clips. Measured on a Mac, not an iPhone.
versions.parakeet-v2-and-parakeet: Parakeet v2 and Parakeet Ultra made fewer mistakes than Apple's recognition, and Ultra was the most accurate. It was also quicker to show a correct word: a median of 0.25 seconds after it was said, against 0.67 seconds for Apple.
versions.accuracy-was-not-the: Accuracy was not the only question. Parakeet Ultra is a big model, and a big download is a cost for every user. So we tried making it smaller, and checked what that does to accuracy.
versions.model-size-against-word: Model size against word error rate for the Parakeet builds
versions.lower-is-better-and: Lower is better, and further left is smaller. Ultra 6-bit is 498 MB at 13.8%, the same accuracy as the 632 MB Ultra 8-bit. Ultra 4-bit is 350 MB at 14.8%. Parakeet v2 is 464 MB at 15.5%. Redux is 220 MB at 16.7%. The v3 4-bit build is 336 MB at 22.7%. A dashed line marks Apple SpeechAnalyzer at 17.2%. Ultra 6-bit, Ultra 4-bit, v2 and Ultra 8-bit all sit below it.
versions.model-size-on-disk: Model size on disk (MB), smaller is left
versions.word-error-rate-lower: Word error rate, lower is better
versions.size-and-word-error: Size and word error rate of the Parakeet builds
versions.lower-is-better-left: Lower is better, left is smaller. The dashed line is Apple SpeechAnalyzer at 17.2% (its model is part of the phone's system, so it does not add to the app's size). Source: engine accuracy report, Size options table, and evidence log E12. Measured on a Mac, not an iPhone.
versions.the-6-bit-version: The 6-bit version is smaller than the published 8-bit build (498 MB instead of 632 MB) and made no more mistakes in our test. The 4-bit version is smaller still (350 MB) and cost about one point of accuracy, though it still beat Apple. The ready-made small builds from others were either less accurate than Apple (Redux) or much worse (v3 4-bit).
versions.it-is-tied-for: It is tied for the fewest mistakes of anything we tested: 13.8 in 100 words, against 17.2 for Apple.
versions.it-is-134-mb: It is 134 MB smaller than the 8-bit version and just as accurate (also 13.8%).
versions.it-is-fast-to: It is fast to show words (median 0.25 s), and it runs on the phone with no internet.
versions.if-it-does-not: If it does not work out on an iPhone, the fallback is Parakeet Ultra 4-bit: smaller (350 MB), about a point less accurate, still better than Apple.
versions.what-we-have-not: What we have not shown yet: these tests ran on a Mac with one set of recordings. The next step is checking on an iPhone. Until then, Seal Speak uses Apple's recognition. The switch arrives in 1.1.0. Captions can still contain mistakes with any engine.
versions.the-full-results-including: The full results, including every accent we tested, are in the engine accuracy report on GitHub. The research note behind the size test is evidence log E12.
versions.how-parakeet-did-in: How Parakeet did in other languages
versions.before-promising-a-language: Before promising a language, we measured it.
versions.fewer-mistakes-than-apple-2: fewer mistakes than Apple in French, 39% in German and 30% in Spanish
versions.we-ran-apple-s: We ran Apple's speech recognition and Parakeet Ultra on the same recordings in Spanish, French and German, and counted mistakes the same way as in the English test: word error rate, with a 95% confidence interval. Lower is better.
versions.word-error-rate-by-3: Word error rate by language and engine
versions.parakeet-made-30-to: Parakeet made 30 to 40% fewer mistakes in every language, and the ranges do not overlap. That is why 1.1.0 uses it.
versions.these-recordings-are-people: These recordings are people reading sentences in quiet rooms, not conversations, so every engine scores much better here than in real life. The ranking is the useful part. Measured on a Mac, not an iPhone. Source: language accuracy report (FLEURS test sets, CC BY 4.0).
versions.how-we-chose-the-2: How we chose the translation engine
versions.three-engines-can-translate: Three engines can translate on the phone with no internet. We tested all three on the same sentences, then tested the winner in every language it offers.
versions.languages-tested-with-apple: languages tested with Apple's translation, 1,012 sentences each
versions.scored-as-well-as: scored as well as Spanish, French and German, where Apple beat both other engines
versions.or-less-to-translate: or less to translate a caption line (median, on a Mac)
versions.we-score-translations-with: We score translations with chrF: how closely a translation matches one written by a person, from 0 to 100. Higher is better. We tested two kinds of text: ordinary written sentences, and the same sentences the way captions arrive, in lower case with no punctuation.
versions.translation-score-chrf-by: Translation score (chrF) by engine, English into each language
versions.apple-s-translation-scored: Apple's translation scored highest everywhere, and it lost the least when the punctuation was missing, which is how captions arrive. All three were fast enough for live captions. That is why 1.1.0 uses Apple's translation.
versions.then-we-ran-apple: Then we ran Apple's translation in all 19 languages it offered on our Mac, on the same 1,012 sentences. Here we add a second score, COMET, from 0 to 1, which judges whether the meaning came across and can be compared between languages. chrF can't: it always runs low for Japanese, Chinese and Korean, which don't put spaces between words.
versions.apple-s-translation-from: Apple's translation from English into 19 languages: chrF, COMET and median time per caption line
versions.18-of-the-19: 18 of the 19 scored a COMET of 0.86 or more, the same range as Spanish, French and German.
versions.hindi-scored-lowest-0: Hindi scored lowest (0.807). It needs a closer look before we offer it.
versions.simplified-chinese-sometimes-ca: Simplified Chinese sometimes came back in Traditional characters, in about 2 of every 100 caption lines. We will check this on an iPhone.
versions.each-language-is-a: Each language is a one-time download of 154 to 291 MB, made by iOS, not by Seal Speak.
versions.which-of-these-languages: Which of these languages 1.1.0 offers is not decided yet.
versions.sentences-from-flores-200: Sentences from FLORES-200 (1,012 per language), written text rather than conversation. Measured on a Mac, not an iPhone. Sources: translation comparison report, with every confidence interval, and results for every language.
versions.seal-speak-is-made: Seal Speak is made by Gil Eskayo. © 2026.
